inputs.prompt:
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the target character. Their complete identity, face, hair, body, and outfit come from <Picture 1>, <Picture 2>, <Picture 3>, and <Picture 4>. <Subject 1> completely replaces the main performer in <Video 1>.
<Subject 2> is the environment shown in <Video 1>.
<Video 1> is the source segment for the target timeline. It defines the motion, poses, timing, performer position, camera movement, framing, and environment for every output frame.

summary:
[video editing] Replace the main performer in <Video 1> with <Subject 1>. Preserve the source timeline, choreography or action, pacing, composition, camera work, and environment one-to-one.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears throughout [Shot 1]): attribute_transfer - complete target-character identity and outfit from the reference pictures replace the source performer. The source performer's body position, pose sequence, movement direction, speed, timing, and rhythm follow <Video 1> one-to-one.
<Subject 2> (appears throughout [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - preserve the environment, lighting, camera work, framing, and shot structure from <Video 1>.
<Video 1> (complete target timeline and shot structure): fully_preserved - its temporal order, motion, pace, framing, and camera path define every physical output frame.

detailed_description:
[Shot 1] <Subject 1> replaces the source performer throughout the shot. Keep the same body scale, ground position, framing, scene geometry, lighting, and camera movement as <Video 1>. Every pose, transition, movement direction, speed, and rhythm follows <Video 1> at the same timestamp. Motion continues naturally without pausing, replaying, compressing time, skipping forward, or anticipating the clip boundary. Keep the background clean and stable without chromatic noise, color blotches, or compression artifacts.

N/A - handle audio separately.
